_about: Stamp duty and registration fee on the sale (conveyance) of a residential property. Only states whose every component was read on an official government page are listed. pct = percent of the property value. womanPct = rate when the buyer is a woman (absent = no concession). Registration: pct of value, roundUpTo = value rounded up to this step first, add = fixed amount added, min/max = limits. A state is published only while retrievedOn is within maxAgeDays.

states.name: Delhi
states.valueBasis: the sale price or the circle rate value, whichever is higher
notes: Rates for a man buying alone (6%) and a woman buying alone (4%) are from the Delhi Revenue Department. It does not state a single rate for joint buyers, so ask the sub-registrar if you are buying jointly.
The registration fee is 1% of the value plus ₹100 pasting fee.

states.name: Maharashtra
states.valueBasis: the market value (ready reckoner rate) or the agreement value, whichever is higher
notes: Stamp duty is set by Article 25 of the Maharashtra Stamp Act. Women buyers get a 1 percentage point reduction (in force since April 2021); conditions apply, so confirm eligibility with the sub-registrar.
The registration fee is ₹100 plus ₹10 for every ₹1,000 above ₹10,000, which works out to about 1%, capped at ₹30,000.
Some municipal corporations add a metro cess on top of stamp duty (see the IGR Maharashtra circulars). It is not included here.

sources.label: IGR Maharashtra: Maharashtra Stamp Act, article-wise (22.07.2026)

states.name: Telangana
states.valueBasis: the market value or the sale price, whichever is higher

areas.label: Municipal or other non-gram panchayat area

notes: Rates are from the Telangana Registration Department's ready reckoner for a sale deed. Telangana does not give women buyers a lower rate.
In both kinds of area the total comes to 7.5% of the value; only the split between transfer duty and registration fee differs.
